title: Guess Resistance Lab
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Assessment Design
Guess-Resistant Probes
Knowledge Tracing
Probability
description: A p5.js lab comparing probe designs by the chance that a pure guesser succeeds on the first attempt (1/options^chained) and the attempts needed to guarantee success when retries are allowed. Sliders set options and chained items, a checkbox allows retry until correct, one guesser's attempt sequence is drawn as a strip of wrong and right squares, and 1000 simulated guessers produce a histogram of attempts used.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: How probe design and retry policy affect lucky guessing
learningObjectives: The learner will compare the chance of a lucky success and the attempts needed to guarantee success across probe designs by changing option count, chained items and retry policy.
prerequisites: The guess parameter of Bayesian knowledge tracing (Chapter 18)

accessibility.notes: All controls are native and labeled; attempt squares carry a check or a cross as well as color; describe() reports the design, the lucky-guess chance, the last guesser's sequence and the 1000-guesser result

controls.label: Chained items
controls.purpose: Number of items that must all be right

controls.label: Allow retry until correct
controls.purpose: Let the guesser try untried combinations until it succeeds

controls.label: Guess randomly
controls.purpose: Simulate one random guesser and draw its attempt sequence

controls.label: Run 1000 guessers
controls.purpose: Draw a histogram of attempts used and report first-attempt successes

simulation.model: Monte Carlo simulation of uniform random guessing without replacement
equations: attempts to guarantee success with retry = options^chained
with retry, attempts used ~ Uniform(1, options^chained)
assumptions: Chained items give feedback only for the whole chain, so a retry is a new combination
The guesser never repeats a combination it has tried

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Parameter exploration with simulation and comparison to reference designs
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Sliders, single-run animation and a 1000-run histogram
keyQuestions: How fast does the lucky-guess chance fall as items are chained?
How many attempts guarantee success when retries are allowed?
What must a record keep so a guesser does not look like a knower?
commonMisconceptions: A correct final answer shows mastery even when retries were allowed
More options always beats chaining items
A low guess rate on paper means the probe resists guessing in practice
